supports: identity: University of Tulsa confirms Presidential Scholarship.
value: Full tuition (excluding summers) for five years or until an undergraduate degree is earned.

application: Apply for admission and the Presidential Scholarship with a one-page resume and short answers; submit official transcripts and required test scores and complete an official campus visit by February 1. A 45-second video and meeting with an admission counselor are strongly suggested.

eligibility: First-year applicants need ACT superscore 28 or SAT 1300, plus one of: College Board Recognition Program scholar in the top 10% of class, top 5% of class, or weighted GPA 4.0 on a 4.0 scale. Schools reporting only unweighted GPA receive individual consideration. Transfer applicants have a separate route requiring a 3.7 college GPA and, for fewer than 30 college credits, qualifying test scores.

supports: identity: National Federation of Music Clubs (NFMC) confirms Lynn Freeman Olson Composition Awards.
value: $1,500 high-school and $750 intermediate awards for further musical study; judges may withhold awards.

application: Follow the award-specific mailed application rules: send the typed signed form, an original manuscript and six legible copies, postmarked by March 1 in an odd year. Do not email or upload. Submit one anonymous piano solo or piano-only ensemble composition, no more than four engraved pages and written for early-elementary to intermediate piano skill. Do not include recordings.

eligibility: Nonprofessional composers in grades 10 to 12 for the $1,500 high-school category, or grades 7 to 9 for the $750 intermediate category, who are currently studying music and are NFMC members. Works must not have been published for public use or sale. Only one original composition per entrant; arrangements are excluded. Past monetary winners cannot reenter the same category. U.S. citizenship is not required.

supports: identity: Georgia Student Finance Commission confirms HOPE Scholarship.

eligibility: Georgia resident under institution rules (normally 12 months if resident at high-school completion, otherwise a 24-month route; dependent/private-school rules differ), U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen, undergraduate degree student at eligible Georgia institution. Meet applicable Selective Service, loan/refund good-standing, drug-free and satisfactory-progress rules. Standard accredited high-school/home-study route: minimum 3.0 calculated HOPE GPA and four academic-rigor credits. Ineligible-school/unaccredited-home-study or TCSG HSE route may qualify by ACT 24 or SAT 1160 before completion without that high-school GPA route. College students may gain eligibility at 30/60/90 semester-hour checkpoints with 3.0 calculated college HOPE GPA.

application: Complete FAFSA annually or online Georgia Student Finance Application (GSFAPP), plus any college-specific steps. Georgia accredited schools electronically report transcripts/rigor data; out-of-state or nonaccredited/home-study routes need official manual-evaluation documents and qualifying test reporting where applicable. Monitor GAfutures eligibility and college financial-aid office.

supports: identity: Tennessee Higher Education Commission and Student Assistance Corporation confirms Tennessee HOPE Scholarship.

value: Up to $2,250 per full-time semester freshman/sophomore and $2,850 junior/senior at four-year institutions or two-year institutions with on-campus housing; up to $1,600 at other two-year institutions. Summer funding available. Generally 75% of full award at 9-11 credits and 50% at 6-8; under six normally not funded, with graduation/programme exceptions. Only courses leading to the eligible associate/bachelor programme are funded.

supports: identity: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education confirms Palmetto Fellows Scholarship.

value: Up to $6,700 freshman year and $7,500 subsequent eligible years toward cost of attendance after other gift aid, half fall/half spring. Normally two terms for one-year certificates, four for associates, eight for first bachelors, ten for approved five-year bachelors. Renewal requires 3.0 institutional GPA, 30 new earned credits annually and continued full-time attendance/residency/certifications. Approved STEM, accounting or education enhancements can add up to $2,500 annually starting sophomore year, normally up to $10,000 combined. Education enhancement requires a teaching-service contract.

supports: identity: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education confirms LIFE Scholarship.

application: College determines eligibility using official final high-school transcript, residency/citizenship verification and any applicable test/rank documentation. Submit required criminal-history and financial-aid default/refund certifications. No FAFSA needed solely for this merit award; other financial aid may need it. deadline: No separate statewide scholarship application. Submit required admission, official academic records and eligibility documents by the college financial-aid office's deadlines; mid-year graduates require additional early-graduation documents.
identity: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education confirms LIFE Scholarship.

value: Up to $5,000 annually at eligible four-year institutions ($4,700 tuition plus $300 book allowance); two-year amounts based on eligible tuition/book costs, capped at $5,000. Cost-of-attendance ceiling applies with other gift aid. Normally two terms for one-year certificates, four for associates, six for approved 68-credit associates, eight for first bachelors, ten for approved five-year degrees. Renewal requires 3.0 LIFE GPA and average 30 earned credits per academic year. Approved STEM, accounting or education majors may add up to $2,500 annually starting sophomore year; education recipients sign a South Carolina public-school teaching obligation.

eligibility: South Carolina resident and U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident at high-school graduation and enrolment; full-time eligible degree student. Four-year freshman route requires two of three: 3.0 unrounded SC Uniform Grading Policy GPA, SAT 1100 or ACT equivalent 22, top 30% approved UGP class rank. Nonranking schools require GPA plus test route. Two-year freshman route requires 3.0 UGP GPA. Eligible SC schools/homeschool or qualified out-of-state dependent route applies; later college eligibility can be earned with LIFE GPA/credit requirements. Enhancement requires approved major and normally 14 eligible math/science/accounting credits by end of first college year; education route has separate service-contract requirements.

supports: identity: Kentucky Higher Education Assistance Authority (KHEAA) confirms Kentucky Educational Excellence Scholarship (KEES).

value: Each qualifying high-school year earns $187 at 2.75 GPA to $500 at 4.00 toward each college year; earned annual base amounts accumulate. Highest pregraduation ACT/SAT bonus up to $500; free/reduced-lunch eligible students can add $200-$300 per qualifying AP/IB/Cambridge examination, with no examination-count cap. Half-time college enrolment minimum; part-time amounts adjusted. Award expires at eight funded semesters, five years after graduation or bachelor degree, whichever first. Separate comprehensive-transition programme awards for students with intellectual disabilities are $250/$500 per term based on load, up to eight terms.

eligibility: Kentucky resident, U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident; not a convicted felon. Certified-school GPA route needs approved curriculum and at least 2.75 in an award-earning year beginning 2026-27. Kentucky homeschool/noncertified-school graduates and qualifying GED recipients (age 18-23) can earn a score-only award, without the school GPA route. Certain Kentucky-resident military dependents, exchange/Page School students and approved programmes outside Kentucky qualify.

application: No separate application for ordinary college route: school reports grades, test results and eligibility; check MyKHEAA records and college financial-aid office. Approved workforce reimbursement instead requires Pathway Selection Form, request form and clear itemised receipts after eligible expenses are paid.

Remedial/graduate courses excluded; student pays uncovered costs. Normally six years after high-school graduation, with military/service/disability extensions. Institution credits account; summer often requires upfront payment and later reimbursement.

supports: identity: West Virginia Higher Education Policy Commission confirms PROMISE Scholarship.

value: Up to $5,500 per year or eligible tuition/mandatory fees, whichever less; maximum determined annually and funding contingent on state appropriations. Institution receives payment for degree-pursuant undergraduate coursework. Up to eight bachelor semesters or four associate semesters; normally must use within six years after award, with military extension. Completion of degree ends eligibility. Renewal normally 2.75 overall college GPA and 30 earned credits per two-semester academic year (15 for one semester), continuous full-time enrolment, with final-year exceptions.

deadline: Class of 2027: Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA open October 1, 2026; both must meet submission/processing conditions by March 1, 2027. Last qualifying SAT administration is June 2027; last qualifying national ACT is July 2027. No time zone stated.

application: Create WVSAM account, verify email, submit Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA by March 1, 2027, even if qualifying grades/scores are still pending. Send individual official test administrations (ACT code 4539, SAT 3456) and monitor matching/status. Public-school academic records generally supplied through school system; private-school final records and special homeschool/commuter/military forms require school/applicant verification. Scholars do not reapply annually; annual FAFSA encouraged for other aid.

First-time full-time initial award normally within two years of graduation, with specified exceptions.

supports: identity: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction and North Dakota University System confirms North Dakota Scholarship.
value: $750 per semester, up to $6,000, usable at approved North Dakota colleges, universities, professional schools and registered apprenticeship programs within six years of graduation.

application: Create/use North Dakota Login and complete Class of 2027 application. School submits Choice Ready eligibility report; nonpublic schools use verification form. Homeschool applicants supply notices of intent for home-education years, notarised grades 9-12 transcript and verification, official test and dual-enrolment records. Tests must be taken before graduation; send later-than-March ACT results to NDDPI code 2927. No annual reapplication after award; institution certifies renewal.

eligibility: North Dakota resident at graduation with ND high-school diploma, including documented homeschool route. Essential Skills: 3.00 overall unweighted GPA, civics test 70%+, nine weeks career education/counselling, four-year rolling plan and four of eight additional indicators. Also complete two of three pathways: Post-Secondary Ready (ACT 24/SAT 1180 plus two approved academic indicators), Workforce Ready (required CTE/language coursework, ACT 24/SAT 1180 or WorkKeys all three scores 5+, plus two workforce indicators), Military Ready (ASVAB 50+, or 31+ with basic training within 90 days after graduation, required PE plus two indicators). ACT superscores allowed. Same dual course cannot satisfy both pathway indicators.

supports: identity: South Dakota Board of Regents confirms South Dakota Opportunity Scholarship.

value: Up to $7,500 total: $1,500 annually first three years, $3,000 fourth year, paid half each fall/spring. Up to eight consecutive fall/spring terms or first bachelor, whichever first. Renewal requires cumulative college GPA 3.00 (checked after second term then every term), persistence and 30/60/90 earned credits before sophomore/junior/senior payments. One GPA reinstatement possible; lost time not extended.
deadline: Official current pages disagree on spring first-time deadline/preferred date; recurring deadlines have no explicit 2027 year/time zone. Confirm category-specific timing.

application: Complete SD Opportunity Scholarship Application in SDBOR Scholarship Portal, using public-university email if already dual-enrolled/enrolled, otherwise create manual account. Same application covers new and transfer students. Current handout says high-school transcript verified through admissions, with no additional transcript submission. Ensure official scores and class-of-2027 curriculum/endorsement are reflected in institutional review; homeschool transcript has separate legal requirements. No annual reapplication normally.

eligibility: South Dakota resident at high-school graduation; enter eligible SD institution within five years, or qualifying military-release extension. Option 1: ACT composite/superscore 24+ or SAT 1180+, 3.00 unweighted GPA and Advanced Honors Endorsement/approved curriculum with final grades C+. Class of 2027 requires specific subject subcategories. Option 2: ACT 28+ with English 18, reading 21, math 22 and science 24 subscores, or Board of Regents SAT equivalent 1310+; no GPA/curriculum requirement. Law and official 2027 guide specify ACT subscores even though overview/handout omit them. Tests before college; separate alternative-instruction route.

supports: identity: Montana University System confirms MUS Honor Scholarship.
value: Four-year renewable tuition waiver at an eligible Montana campus (average value about $5,000 a year at a 4-year campus); does not cover mandatory or class fees. Up to 200 awarded annually.

deadline: Applications open December 1, 2026. Complete application, college acceptance, score proof, official seventh-semester transcript and signed certification by March 15, 2027. Take ACT/SAT by February 2027; superscores may include only tests by then. School submits eligible GPA rankings by annual March 15 deadline. No time zone stated.

application: Apply to and be accepted at eligible Montana campus, then complete AwardMontana online application. Upload acceptance letter/email, official seventh-semester transcript covering freshman through first senior semester, ACT/SAT proof and counselor-signed Rigorous Core/IB/Attendance Certification. Middle-school transcript required if counting Algebra I from middle school; other courses must appear on high-school transcript. Accept/decline promptly if offered.

eligibility: Montana resident/U.S. citizen applying in graduation year, normally three full-time years at Montana Board-accredited high school including senior year. Narrow military-parent exception permits prior out-of-state accredited schooling with Montana senior year and documented parent residency/support. Seventh-semester GPA 3.40+ using school weighting consistently; complete Rigorous Core or IB diploma by graduation. Selection combines within-school GPA rank points (rounded tenth) and ACT/SAT equivalent, with ACT superscores accepted by February 2027. Accepted eligible campus required; minimums do not guarantee award.
